conventions.convention: The wave operator is W=c⁻²∂t²−Δ, so □c=c²W. The source contribution to its Cauchy solution carries c². Closed-slab smoothness means restriction from a smooth function on R³×J for an open interval J containing the slab.

Unit-sphere surface measure has mass 4π; spherical harmonics are real and orthonormal for that unnormalised measure, with m=1,…,2l+1. Solid coefficient factors at y=0 use their homogeneous polynomial extensions.

On S_R the orthonormal basis is Y^R_lm(Rn)=R⁻¹Y_lm(n). DtN pairings are linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second. Rough outgoingness means outgoing h_l radial factors with no incoming partners, not a pointwise Sommerfeld condition.
The outgoing radial factor uses e^{ikr}; t_l=kh_l′(kR)/h_l(kR), with −(l+1)/R≤Re t_l≤−1/R and 0<Im t_l≤k. In degree zero, t_0=ik−1/R.

The smooth PEC space X is the curl/div graph-norm closure of smooth ambient fields with ν×u=0; V consists of its divergence-free fields and H is the L² closure of V. No equality with every maximal tangential-trace realization is asserted. Zero modes are retained.

For transmission, n points from minus to plus, [W]=W_+−W_−, and n·[ε∇u]=−σ. Thus the explicitly defined flux D=−ε∇u satisfies n·[D]=σ. Neumann compatibility and zero-mean normalization are componentwise.
In the truncated exterior, the inner-boundary normal points into the obstacle. It is extended constantly along normal collar lines; κ=div n and the closure condition is ∂nE_n+κE_n=−div∂O e_T.

Causal transforms use χ(z)=∫₀∞K(s)e^{izs}ds, matching histories e^{−iωt}. Principal values use symmetric exclusion around ω, with absolutely convergent tails. Instantaneous or declared polynomial response is subtracted before applying the corresponding dispersion formulas.

Retarded-root claims require an all-time history z:R→R³ with one uniform speed bound v_*<c. Differentiability is asserted off x=z(t), and higher regularity follows only from the corresponding higher regularity of z.
The particle calculation uses η=diag(−1,1,1,1), indices 0 through 3, F_νμ=∂νA_μ−∂μA_ν, τ′=√(−η(X′,X′))/c and U=X′/τ′. It is a deduction about a chosen functional, not adoption of a physical action.
Carleman weights use integer s≥1 and τ=s+1; the H² extension is restricted to support away from the origin. Fourier differentiation uses the 2π convention.
The bounded-error comparison is deterministic and conditional on simultaneous recorded-value and calibration bounds. It supplies neither a sampling law nor statistical confidence.

load_bearing.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For a real Hilbert space H, a symmetric bounded bilinear form a with a(v,v)≥α‖v‖² for α>0, and a bounded linear functional ℓ, there is exactly one u∈H satisfying a(u,v)=ℓ(v) for every v∈H, and ‖u‖≤‖ℓ‖/α.

Assume AC. For bounded open Ω⊆(−L,L)³, L>0, H¹ is complete, its zero-boundary closure H¹₀ is closed and complete, the quadratic Sobolev norm is Hilbert, and ‖v‖²₂≤(2L)²‖∂₁v‖²₂≤(2L)²‖∇v‖²₂ for every v∈H¹₀. The gradient and full H¹ norms are equivalent there.

Assume Countable Choice. For real homogeneous polynomials P_l on R³ and H_l=ker Δ, P_l=H_l⊕|x|²P_{l−2}, dim H_l=2l+1, distinct degrees are orthogonal on S², their union admits a complete orthonormal L² basis, and every real orthonormal degree-l basis satisfies Σ_mY_lm(n)Y_lm(n′)=(2l+1)P_l(n·n′)/(4π).

Assume Countable Choice, c>0, t₀<T, smooth whole-space data a,b and an extension-sense smooth source h. The displayed spherical-mean solution u=∂sH_a+H_b+c²∫ₜ₀ᵗH_{h(·,v)}(x,t−v)dv is extension-sense smooth, solves Wu=h and attains data (a,b); it is unique among extension-sense C² solutions. Agreement on the closed base ball and backward cone gives agreement at the vertex. If all three supports lie in one ball of radius ρ, u(x,t)=0 for |x|>ρ+c(t−t₀).

Assume AC and the stated Countable Choice interfaces. On a bounded smooth domain, smooth uniformly positive symmetric coefficients, smooth bulk data and smooth Dirichlet or compatible Neumann data give a weak solution smooth on the closure. For finitely many disjoint closed smooth interior interfaces with piecewise smooth positive coefficients and bulk data and smooth sheet charge, the weak solution is smooth on each closed side; edges, junctions, reentrant corners and coefficient loss of regularity are excluded.

Assume AC, k,R>0. The spherical modal operator T_R is bounded H^{1/2}(S_R)→H^{−1/2}(S_R), with Re⟨T_Rf,f⟩≤0 and Im⟨T_Rf,f⟩=Σ_lm(Im t_l)|f_lm|²>0 for f≠0. For every H^{1/2} trace, its outgoing h_l series is the unique solution in the declared outgoing finite-local-energy modal class, with weak normal derivative T_Rf, smooth away from the sphere; smooth traces satisfy ordinary Sommerfeld radiation.

Assume AC and a bounded smooth domain. For the declared graph completion X, divergence-free V and H=closure of V in L², the curl form has a complete orthonormal H eigenbasis, nonnegative finite-multiplicity eigenvalues tending to infinity when H is infinite dimensional, and a finite-dimensional retained zero sector. Every eigenfield satisfies the variational identity for all v∈X. For q₀∈V, q₁∈H and any positive mathematical wave speed, the modal wave converges in C(K;V) for displacement and C(K;H) for velocity on compact time intervals, with affine zero modes.

Assume AC and a bounded smooth domain. Every real f∈L² has a unique u∈H¹₀∩H² satisfying ∫(∇u·∇v+uv)=∫fv for all v∈H¹₀, with ‖u‖H¹≤‖f‖₂ and ‖u‖H²≤CΩ‖f‖₂. Smooth ambient zero-boundary functions are H²-dense in H²∩H¹₀; their gradients converge in the curl/div graph norm, so ∇u belongs to the declared PEC completion.

Assume AC and the stated Countable Choice interfaces. For a bounded smooth domain, constant ε>0, open interval J, jointly smooth bulk data and smooth boundary families, the Dirichlet Poisson problem has a unique smooth family with one smooth ambient continuation. The Neumann problem has such a family exactly when ∫Ω_j f+∫∂Ω_j κ=0 for each component at every time; zero componentwise means give uniqueness. The solution operations are linear and commute with time differentiation, with estimates local on compact time intervals.

For c>0 and an all-time C¹ history z:R→R³ with |z′|≤v_*<c, every (x,t) has exactly one root t−s=|x−z(s)|/c, with s≤t and equality exactly when x=z(t). Off that graph, s is C¹, r=c(t−s)>0, κ=1−n·z′(s)/c lies between 1−v_*/c and 1+v_*/c, and s_t=1/κ, ∇s=−n/(cκ). A C^k history gives a C^k root there; a merely C¹ history need not give C².

Assume Countable and Dependent Choice. For a real locally absolutely continuous matrix kernel K on [0,∞) with K,K′,sK∈L¹ entrywise, χ(z)=∫K(s)e^{izs}ds has holomorphic upper-half-plane entries, continuous closed-half-plane values and C¹ real boundary values, satisfies |χ_jk(z)|≤(|K_jk(0)|+‖K′_jk‖₁)/|z| for nonzero closed-half-plane z, and obeys the stated two entrywise principal-value dispersion formulas. Instantaneous real response is subtracted; passivity is separate.

concerns.concern: Proof 3.3, items/thm-em-spherical-multipole-basis.md:93, writes r^(−l−1)∫|y|^l P_l(n·y/|y|)ρ(y)dy = ∫ρ(y)|x|^(−l−1)P_l(x·y/(|x||y|))dy. The right-hand integral drops |y|^l. This is a false equality for general admitted densities: take l=1, x=4e₁ and a nonnegative smooth density supported near 2e₁ inside B₃. The left integrand has an additional positive factor |y|>1. The asserted homogeneous extension at y=0 also belongs to the weighted coefficient, not the displayed unweighted one. The theorem's conclusion is not refuted, but this written computation requires correction.

Statement (c), items/thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence.md:49, defines [ε∇u]=ε⁺∇u⁺−ε⁻∇u⁻ but calls it 'the difference from the n-positive side to the other'. That wording reverses the direction of the displayed plus-minus subtraction and the supplier's normal from minus to plus. The formula and proof use the correct sign; the explanatory wording is inconsistent.

alerts.finding: Fact F1(d), items/pthm-em-general-wave-ivp.md:174, restates the supplier as: 'if a,b vanish off compact sets and h(·,v) vanishes off a fixed compact set contained in [the ball of radius ρ], then u(x,t)=0 whenever |x|>ρ+c(t−t₀)'. The cited thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff(d) requires K_a∪K_b∪K_h⊆that ball. The restatement omits containment of the initial-data supports. As written it already fails at t=t₀: take h=b=0, ρ=1 and a smooth nonzero bump near 10e₁. Proof 6.3 separately checks the correct support containment, but that does not make the stated Fact faithful.

Fact F6, items/pthm-em-gauge-reachability.md:93, locates lem-em-parameter-dependent-smooth-poisson-boundary-solvers 'on the wave-equation prerequisites page'. Its actual home is em-expanded-analysis-prerequisites, as both the group task and that page's item inventory show. The quoted mathematical interface otherwise retains the supplier's hypotheses and conclusions.

seams_checked.note: Structural page prerequisite; no owned item cites either of its two homed variational items. Opened the page, fundamental variation lemma and localization supplier; no strengthened proposition is asserted across this edge.

Particle variation retains future timelike C² curves, one-sided endpoint calculus, τ′=√(−η(X′,X′))/c, U=X′/τ′ and η(U,U)=−c². It imports mathematical definitions/results without importing clock postulates.
Particle variation uses the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski model and future positive orthonormal inertial chart with signature (−,+,+,+), matching the opened definitions.

The existence and uniqueness consumers preserve bounded smooth domains, constant positive ε₀I, componentwise Neumann compatibility, finite closed interior interfaces, exact prescribed traces and n·[ε∇u]=−σ. No prescribed-total-conductor-charge existence is attributed to the supplier.

The general multipole consumer preserves compact L¹ density support, r>a, the geometric degree tail, all-order differentiation on exterior compacta and the separate L² ball branch. Supplier Proof 3.3 has the owned concern recorded above; the consumer restatement retains the weighted moments correctly.

Newtonian consumers retain smooth compact data; thin-loop consumers retain embedded C² arc-length closed curves and distinguish off-curve convergence from separately supplied global distributional identities. Magnetic dipole estimates preserve r≥2a and the differentiated explicit remainder.

The bounded gauge branch explicitly uses the dedicated parameter-dependent Poisson supplier, retaining smooth graph domains, smooth families, componentwise compatibility, normalization and auxiliary ambient extensions. The supplier's page-location error is separately alerted.

The slab branch consumes Kirchhoff through lem-em-gauge-wave-reachability: whole-space extension-sense smooth data, zero gauge Cauchy data and Wχ=G. It does not attribute arbitrary bounded-domain Lorenz boundary solvability to the wave theorem.

pthm-em-general-wave-ivp F1(d) omits containment of the initial-data supports in the radius-ρ ball when restating the supplier's propagation bound. Other checked Cauchy, uniqueness and cone clauses match; Proof 6.3 checks the correct containment. Routed the false Fact as an alert.

Radiation Fact F8 and Proof 3.1 preserve the c² Duhamel factor for W, zero initial data and extension-sense smooth sources; potential source normalizations are μ₀c²ρ and μ₀J_k. The additional integrable-dispersion citation also preserves K,K′,sK∈L¹ and Countable/Dependent Choice.

thm-em-uncertainty-analysis F24 preserves the nondegenerate interval, f(θ₀)=0, derivative lower bound m>0 and simultaneous recorded/calibration bounds. Its line restriction supplies those hypotheses and retains a deterministic conditional conclusion.

Gauge, retarded-kernel and forced-Maxwell consumers preserve extension-sense smooth slab data, W normalization, the c² source factor, C² uniqueness and the closed cone. Retarded-kernel identification uses compact spacetime sources and a time below their support; it does not assert smoothness of the kernel itself.
